entries.message: "./.github/actions/validate-semver" is looked up in the workspace at run time, where an earlier step can replace it. use the self-repository syntax "$/.github/actions/validate-semver" which always refers to the commit running the workflow

"npm install" takes the newest release of every dependency, however new, so a compromised release reaches the workflow before it is found and pulled. pass `--min-release-age=7` or set `min-release-age=7` in .npmrc (npm 11.10 and later)

command "npm install" installs a package outside of a lock file: its dependencies are resolved anew on every run, although its version is pinned. add the package to package.json and commit the package-lock.json and install with `npm ci`
shellcheck reported issue in this script: SC2016:info:5:10: Expressions don't expand in single quotes, use double quotes for that

action "actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a" (checked as "actions/upload-artifact@v4": the version comment "# v4.6.2" says so, and nothing verifies the comment) declares the Node.js runtime "node20" in its metadata, but Node.js 20 was removed from GitHub Actions on 2026-09-23, so the runner runs the action on Node.js 24 instead of the runtime it declares. update the action to "actions/upload-artifact@v6" or newer, which declares "node24"
job "image-build" needs "validate-version" but never reads its outputs or result, and it already needs "seed-cache" which waits for "validate-version". this entry changes nothing and can be removed

docker/setup-buildx-action restores a cache although the job pushes an image, so a poisoned cache entry can end up in the published artifacts. set "cache-binary: false", or set "cache-mode: none" on the job

secret "DOCKER_HUB_USERNAME" is used by a job which has no "environment:", so it is a repository or organization secret exposed to every job. move it to an environment with protection rules and set "environment:" at the job

secret "DOCKER_HUB_TOKEN" is used by a job which has no "environment:", so it is a repository or organization secret exposed to every job. move it to an environment with protection rules and set "environment:" at the job

docker/build-push-action restores a cache although the job pushes an image, so a poisoned cache entry can end up in the published artifacts. remove the "cache-from" input, or set "cache-mode: none" on the job

workflow has no "concurrency:", so every run of it executes at the same time even when a newer run supersedes the older ones. add a top-level "concurrency:" with a "group:" and "cancel-in-progress: true"

workflow has no "concurrency:", so every run of it executes at the same time even when a newer run supersedes the older ones. add a top-level "concurrency:" with a "group:" and "cancel-in-progress: true". use a group per pull request such as "${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}", so that a new push cancels only the older runs of the same pull request and not the runs of the others
